- Canonical name: T3 Code (`claim-t3-code-sf-identity`)
- Current status: early-stage public product; Latest checked release v0.0.33 (`claim-t3-code-sf-status-early`, `claim-t3-code-sf-beta-terms`, `claim-t3-code-sf-version`, `claim-t3-code-sf-maintenance`)
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-15
- Vendor: LICENSE `T3 Tools Inc.` (`claim-t3-code-sf-vendor`); Terms `T3 Tools, Inc.` (`claim-t3-code-sf-vendor-legal`). GitHub org `pingdotgg` is the repository owner, not these vendor strings.
- Canonical URL: `https://t3.codes/` (`claim-t3-code-sf-canonical-url`)

- Availability: Windows, macOS, Linux desktop; `npx` CLI; iOS; Android (`claim-t3-code-sf-availability`, README; not install.md)

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: an open-source control plane / agent-harness control surface for installed coding-agent CLIs (`claim-t3-code-sf-what-it-is`, `claim-t3-code-sf-primary-type`, `claim-t3-code-sf-wraps-cli-readme`).
- What it is not: a shipped provider CLI or a token reseller (`claim-t3-code-sf-what-it-is-not`, `claim-t3-code-sf-not-resell-tokens`). That it is not a standalone coding-agent runtime is an inference from those facts (`claim-t3-code-sf-not-for-runtime-buyers`).

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `control-plane` (`claim-t3-code-sf-primary-type`)
- Secondary role: `orchestrator` (`claim-t3-code-sf-secondary-role-orchestrator`)
- Agent-loop owner: the wrapped provider CLI is the agent runtime that does the work; T3 clients dispatch orchestration commands (`claim-t3-code-sf-agent-loop-owner`).
- Architecture: a T3 server owns sessions, workspaces, VCS, terminals, and filesystem; web, desktop, and mobile clients use one authenticated Effect RPC WebSocket (`claim-t3-code-sf-architecture`).

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-t3-code-cli`, `surface-t3-code-desktop`, `surface-t3-code-local-web`, `surface-t3-code-hosted-web`, `surface-t3-code-ios`, `surface-t3-code-android`, `surface-t3-code-ios-tailscale`, `surface-t3-code-android-tailscale`, `surface-t3-code-connect-relay`, `surface-t3-code-desktop-remote`, `surface-t3-code-web-lan`, `surface-t3-code-desktop-ssh`, `surface-t3-code-private-network`, `surface-t3-code-generic-ssh`
- Execution location: the user-controlled machine that runs the T3 server (`claim-t3-code-sf-execution-location`).

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: inferred that models belong to the selected wrapped harness (`claim-t3-code-sf-model-strategy`, evidence class `inference`). The site claims mid-thread model switching (`claim-t3-code-sf-tag-model-switching`). Local models: unknown.
- Auth strategy: reuse installed provider CLI logins / subscriptions; Clerk for T3 Connect on web/desktop/mobile; Clerk for T3 accounts with local/direct use without an account; one-time pairing tokens for remote sessions; optional Codex and Claude provider environment variables including API keys (`claim-t3-code-sf-auth-provider-cli`, `claim-t3-code-sf-subscription-reuse`, `claim-t3-code-sf-auth-connect-clerk`, `claim-t3-code-sf-auth-clerk-privacy`, `claim-t3-code-sf-auth-pairing`, `claim-t3-code-sf-auth-optional-env-keys`, `claim-t3-code-sf-auth-optional-env-keys-claude`).
- Provider support: Codex CLI, Claude Code, Cursor CLI (`cursor-agent`), Grok Build CLI, OpenCode (`claim-t3-code-sf-provider-support`).

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: Full access is recommended for disposable worktrees or sandboxes; permission modes are translated onto each provider’s own sandbox/approval settings (`claim-t3-code-sf-isolation-worktrees`, `claim-t3-code-sf-isolation-provider-sandbox`). Worktree definition is `claim-t3-code-sf-worktrees`.
- Permissions: Supervised, Auto-accept edits, Auto, Full access; default new thread is Full access (`claim-t3-code-sf-permission-modes`)
- Security: shared responsibility between T3 Tools-operated infrastructure and the user-controlled host (`claim-t3-code-sf-security`)
- Data path: Terms say User Content is ordinarily processed in the user-controlled environment and selected providers; Privacy says prompts and files go to user-chosen providers; T3 Tools says it does not train AI models on user content (`claim-t3-code-sf-data-path`, `claim-t3-code-sf-data-path-privacy`, `claim-t3-code-sf-no-ai-training`)
